issues.legal_issue: An assessee may change the selected method for computing agricultural income by filing a valid subsequent, fresh, or revised return before assessment is completed.
material_facts: The governing provision gave the assessee a choice between two methods of computing agricultural income.
The original restriction on changing the choice was removed, and the requirement to make the declaration only with the first return was deleted.
The assessee filed a later return with a declaration selecting the other method before the assessment was completed.
issues.conclusion: The assessee was not bound by the method selected with its first return and could change its selection through a valid later return filed before assessment.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6(1) of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948, read with Rule 5 of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Rules, 1949, a declaration indicating the selected method must accompany the return. After removal of the original restriction in section 6(1) and deletion of the word “first” from Rule 5, the declaration could accompany any valid return contemplated by section 15. The Court noted that Kr. Jyoti Sarup v. Board of Revenue, U.P. had interpreted the earlier provisions as restricting changes, but those restrictions were subsequently removed.

rule.if: agricultural_income_assessment and multiple_computation_methods_available and valid_later_return_with_method_declaration and assessment_not_completed

predicates.agricultural_income_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of a taxpayer's agricultural income.
predicates.multiple_computation_methods_available: The applicable assessment scheme offers the taxpayer alternative methods for computing income.
predicates.valid_later_return_with_method_declarati: The taxpayer submits a valid subsequent, fresh, or revised return accompanied by a declaration selecting a computation method.
predicates.assessment_not_completed: The taxpayer submits the later return before the assessment is completed.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income assessment offers alternative computation methods and the taxpayer submits a valid later return with a method declaration before assessment is completed, the taxpayer may change the computation method.

issues.legal_issue: A timely fresh return filed in response to an individual return notice may state a changed computation choice, and earlier participation in the assessment does not waive that choice.
material_facts: The assessee had filed earlier returns selecting one computation method.
After receiving an individual notice requiring a return, the assessee filed a fresh return selecting the other method and accompanying it with the required declaration.
The assessing authority treated the fresh return as having been filed within time and rejected it because it considered the assessee unable to change its choice.
The assessee had earlier produced evidence and inspected the assessment record.
issues.conclusion: The later return was a fresh return filed in response to the notice, not a revised return; the assessee could change its choice in that return, and its earlier participation did not amount to waiver or acquiescence.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 15(3) and 15(4) of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948, a valid fresh return filed within the time specified in an individual notice may carry a new method declaration. A return under section 15(4) must be based on discovery of a wrong statement in the earlier return; merely having selected a different computation method does not constitute such a wrong statement. Earlier production of evidence or inspection of records does not by itself waive the right to make a fresh declaration with a valid later return.

rule.if: agricultural_income_assessment and fresh_return_in_response_to_individual_notice and return_filed_within_allowed_time and later_return_selects_different_method

predicates.agricultural_income_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of a taxpayer's agricultural income.
predicates.fresh_return_in_response_to_individual_n: The taxpayer submits a fresh return in response to an individual notice requiring a return.
predicates.return_filed_within_allowed_time: The fresh return is filed within the applicable filing period or an authorized extension.
predicates.later_return_selects_different_method: The fresh return declares a computation method different from the one selected in an earlier return.

issues.definition: If a taxpayer in an agricultural-income assessment files a timely fresh return in response to an individual notice and selects a different method, the taxpayer may change the method in that return.

issues.legal_issue: A best-judgment assessment must have due regard to the provisional income estimate even if the taxpayer previously selected a computation method.
material_facts: The assessing authority made a best-judgment assessment after the taxpayer failed to satisfy it with the evidence produced.
The authority had sent the taxpayer a provisional estimate of agricultural income computed using one of the available methods.
The authority made its assessment using the method the taxpayer had selected earlier.
issues.conclusion: In a best-judgment assessment, the authority must have due regard to the provisional estimate notwithstanding the taxpayer's selected method, and it may choose an appropriate basis for determining income, including different bases for different parts of the agricultural area.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(4), read with sections 15(3-B) and 6(1) and (2) of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948, requires a best-judgment assessment to be made with due regard to the provisional estimate notwithstanding any method selected by the taxpayer. The estimate must therefore be considered, but the selected method is not binding in such an assessment; the authority may use an appropriate basis, including different bases for different parts of the land.

predicates.agricultural_income_assessment: The proceeding concerns assessment of a taxpayer's agricultural income.
predicates.best_judgment_assessment: The assessing authority determines income to the best of its judgment after the taxpayer fails to make a required return or provide required evidence.
predicates.provisional_income_estimate_provided: The assessing authority has provided the taxpayer with a provisional estimate of income.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income assessment is made to the best of the authority's judgment and a provisional estimate was provided, the authority must consider the estimate but may choose an appropriate computation basis.
